## Synthesizable subsets and SystemC-to-RTL translation

The top priority for svcc: what the synthesizable subsets of SystemC (IEEE 1666.1) and SystemVerilog actually are, and the tools that translate cycle-accurate SystemC into RTL. These define the constructs a design-model conversion must accept, reject, or lower.

Paywalled and not yet read; it must be read and positioned against before submission. |

## Formal and simulation semantics of Verilog and SystemC

Accurate conversion needs a precise account of both sides' scheduling semantics: blocking versus nonblocking assignment, delta cycles, four-state values, and where simulation and synthesis disagree.

| Key | Paper | Year | Venue | Priority | Access | Relevance to svcc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `loow2025simsem` | [The Simulation Semantics of Synthesisable Verilog](https://doi.org/10.1145/3720484)<br>Andreas Lööw | 2025 | PACMPL 9 (OOPSLA1), 2025 | core | [open PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2502.19348) | Formal simulation semantics for exactly the synthesizable Verilog fragment, with attention to blocking/nonblocking scheduling. The best available specification for what svcc must preserve on the SV side. |
| `chen2023essence` | [The Essence of Verilog: A Tractable and Tested Operational Semantics for Verilog](https://doi.org/10.1145/3622805)<br>Qinlin Chen et al. | 2023 | PACMPL 7 (OOPSLA2), 2023 | core | [open PDF](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3622805) | Tractable, tested operational semantics for Verilog's event scheduling, validated against simulators. A reference for the SV scheduling regions svcc maps onto SystemC delta cycles. |
| `mueller2001simsem` | [The simulation semantics of SystemC](https://doi.org/10.1109/date.2001.915002)<br>Wolfgang Mueller et al. | 2001 | DATE 2001 | core | link only | Abstract-state-machine definition of the SystemC scheduler (evaluate, update, delta notification). The SystemC counterpart to the Verilog semantics papers. |
| `cummings2000nba` | [Nonblocking Assignments in Verilog Synthesis, Coding Styles That Kill!](http://www.sunburst-design.com/papers/CummingsSNUG2000SJ_NBA.pdf)<br>Clifford E. Cummings | 2000 | SNUG San Jose 2000 | core | [open copy](http://www.sunburst-design.com/papers/CummingsSNUG2000SJ_NBA.pdf) | The standard practitioner account of blocking versus nonblocking assignment and the race conditions each coding style causes. These are the cases an SV-to-SystemC mapping (sc_signal write versus variable assignment) must get right. |
| `mills1999mismatch` | [RTL Coding Styles That Yield Simulation and Synthesis Mismatches](http://www.sunburst-design.com/papers/CummingsSNUG1999SJ_SynthMismatch.pdf)<br>Don Mills, Clifford E. Cummings | 1999 | SNUG San Jose 1999 | core | [open copy](http://www.sunburst-design.com/papers/CummingsSNUG1999SJ_SynthMismatch.pdf) | Catalog of RTL styles where simulation and synthesis disagree (incomplete sensitivity lists, full_case/parallel_case, X handling). ## Translation validation and compiler correctness

Per-run validation of a compiler's output versus verified compilers, applied to software compilers and to HLS. This is the methodological basis for svcc's checked translation.

| Key | Paper | Year | Venue | Priority | Access | Relevance to svcc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
